question.problem:
Which of the following are stochastic matrices?

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0.1 & 0.7 \\ 0.9 & 0.3\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}0.45 & 0.35 \\ 0.25 & 0.65\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

current_example.problem:
Which of the following are stochastic matrices?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228502/assets/22a6de5cc5918f9cc95ce795f4e0a1c7badb6b70878b4c40dce2b6011860c86f.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that a stochastic vector is a vector with nonnegative entries that add up to $1.$ A matrix is stochastic if all its columns are stochastic vectors.

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices in turn.

- Matrix $\bf{U}$ is *not* a stochastic matrix since its first column is not a stochastic vector (it contains negative entries): 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-0.2 & 0 \\ 1.2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- Matrix $\bf{V}$ is a stochastic matrix. Indeed, each column is a stochastic vector (the corresponding entries are nonnegative and add up to one): 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}0.35 & 0.95 \\ 0.65 & 0.05\end{aligned}]\,\begin{aligned}0.35+0.65=1 \\ 0.95+0.05=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

- Matrix $\bf{W}$ is *not* a stochastic matrix since its third column is not a stochastic vector (the corresponding entries don't add up to one): 

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0.5 & 0 & 0.4 \\ 0.5 & 0 & 0.7\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$\bf{V}$ only."
